R2-003: Runtime C and C++ code must not manage Kotlin object lifetime with raw malloc or free.
CRT finalizer startup is two-phase: NotifyStarted precedes attachCurrentThread, and finalizerThreadIsRunning_ is not a live-thread probe.
Stopping GC work, destroying the runtime, and waiting for finalizers are distinct shutdown steps; a checked-shutdown count includes the finalizer.
CRT_Pin and CRT_UnPin are gated by checkUseCRT; non-CRT targets are intentional no-ops, so a new pin entry must update the CRTStubs no-op stub.
Pin granularity is a GC region, not a single object; a pin prevents region evacuation but is not itself a GC root.
Latin1 String pinning may replace the object with a UTF-16 copy; GCPin, get/addressOf, and GCUnpin must all use the same object.
A static archive must not embed libcrt.so; the final executable or shared library links CRT, and static-archive consumers add that dependency.
R2-003: Never manage Kotlin object lifetime with raw malloc or free; allocate through runtime APIs.
CMC write barriers shade the new reference, but atomic paths enqueue the old value; classify coverage by entry point, not by the SatbBuffer name.

Stack references are intentionally unbarriered while global and heap references need barriers. Removing slot healing or a read barrier requires proving every reader of each GC-visible slot is still covered.
A raw-pointer region is exempt from evacuation while its pin count is non-zero; one pin blocks the whole region, and unpinning only restores collection candidacy.
Moving-GC no-copy defects: re-derive string and array data pointers after any allocation or safepoint; a stale pointer can read from-space data and still exit 0.
Weak references are a tag bit under CMC, and a weak read goes through a safepoint-capable read barrier that may park; Kotlin-to-runtime weak entries need boundary coverage.
CMC phase transitions are driven only by MarkingCollector::TransitionToGCPhase, and each phase installs its own barrier; a phase mismatch silently disables the intended barrier.
Never infer barrier behavior from a symbol or buffer name; verify the concrete access path and, for emitted code, the final IR or disassembly.

A reference that crosses a safepoint stays in addrspace(1); address-space casts stay inseparable from their use, and helpers must not default to AS0.
ObjHolder keeps a root alive but does not keep cached string or array data addresses stable; re-derive interior pointers after allocation or pin with EnterPinScope.
RUNTIME_SWITCH selects SAFEPOINT_EXPANSION_NONE; do not describe retained prologue and loop-body stubs as one PrologueStub, and do not add a second K2R boundary around an expanded safepoint.
Verify declared symbols, IR, object files, and final dynamic symbols separately; a source definition or used attribute does not prove ABI visibility or that LTO and DCE kept the symbol.
CXX1-001: Default to RAII; use unique_ptr for ownership and shared_ptr only for genuinely shared lifetimes.
CXX1-002: Business logic avoids raw new and delete; every early return path releases acquired resources.
CXX2-001: string_view and span do not own data; the owner must outlive the view.
CXX2-002: Never return a string_view or span into a temporary or an object that dies at return.
CXX2-003: A lambda that escapes its scope captures by value, not by reference to a dying local.
CXX3-001: Resource-owning types follow the Rule of 0/3/5; prefer standard containers to express ownership.
CXX3-002: Non-copyable resources such as sockets explicitly delete copy construction and copy assignment.
CXX5-001: Destructors are noexcept; exceptions must not escape a destructor.
CXX6-001: Shared mutable state is guarded by std::mutex with lock_guard or by std::atomic.
CXX6-003: Multiple locks use one consistent acquisition order.
CXX7-001: Reserve known sizes for vector and string growth in hot paths.
Validate signed-to-size_t conversion, multiplication overflow, alignment, and element count before allocation or indexing.
Trace each acquired resource to its matching release on normal, error, early-return, and half-initialized paths.
KC1-001: Do not abuse the null assertion operator; prefer safe calls, Elvis, require/check, or early return.
KC3-001: Keep compiler internals internal or private; do not expose compiler-only types as public API.
KC3-002: New public API considers binary compatibility for KGP, IDE, and plugins; breaking changes document migration.
KC4-002: when over a sealed type is exhaustive, and a new subtype updates every related when.
KC5-002: IR visitors and transformers visit the whole subtree they claim to handle; missed children silently lose semantics.
KC5-003: After an IR transform, maintain parent-child links and transformChildren consistency; do not retain detached nodes.
KC6-001: Shared mutable caches in parallel compilation use thread-safe structures or explicit synchronization.
KC6-002: Avoid coarse synchronized blocks on compilation hot paths; narrow the critical section.
KC7-001: Never swallow Throwable or Exception; record context or convert the failure to a compiler diagnostic.
KC8-001: Compiler and IDE test changes update golden txt/fir/ir data; do not change implementation without expected output.
KC8-002: New diagnostics include positive and negative test cases.
KC10-003: Use the project logger; no println or System.out on hot paths.
